annotation_description: With a hand containing Necrodominance (BBB) and Sheoldred (2BB) — both powerful but slow cards — along with Thoughtseize and Fatal Push for interaction, choosing to be on the draw gives the opponent the initiative. This hand wants to deploy Necrodominance on turn 3, and being on the play would let you Thoughtseize turn 1 before the opponent can deploy threats, then land Necrodominance a full turn earlier relative to the opponent's development. Against an aggressive Izzet deck with cards like Dragon's Rage Channeler and Slickshot Show-Off, being on the draw means the opponent gets to develop first and potentially deal significant damage before Necrodominance or Sheoldred come online.

Playing Thundering Falls tapped on turn 1 instead of Steam Vents means the player cannot cast Dragon's Rage Channeler on turn 1. DRC is one of the best possible turn 1 plays in this archetype, as it enables early surveil triggers and can become a 3/3 flyer. With Steam Vents (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped), the player could cast DRC immediately. The Thundering Falls could then be played tapped on turn 2 when the player likely wants to plot Slickshot Show-Off (which costs 1R and wouldn't be castable off just Thundering Falls + Steam Vents on turn 2 anyway since Thundering Falls only makes U/R). Actually, on turn 2 with Steam Vents (R) + Thundering Falls (R), they'd have 1R available to plot Slickshot or cast Cori-Steel Cutter. Playing Steam Vents untapped turn 1 for DRC, then Thundering Falls tapped turn 2 still gives access to 1R on turn 2 for plotting Slickshot. This is a clearly better sequence.

chosen_display: Cast with alternative cost: Exile two black cards from your hand (source: <font color='#696969' object_id='eaa78d80-9844-4121-85b2-0c7ac72a7cfe'>Soul Spike</font> [eaa])
annotation_description: On turn 1 with no lands in play and 7 mana needed to hardcast Soul Spike, the player chose to exile two black cards from hand to pay the alternative cost. The only black cards in hand are Necrodominance, Fatal Push, Thoughtseize, and Sheoldred, the Apocalypse. Exiling any two of these is catastrophic - these are the deck's best cards. Necrodominance is the engine card, Sheoldred is the win condition, Thoughtseize is key disruption, and Fatal Push is essential removal. Spending 3 cards (Soul Spike + 2 exiled) to deal 4 damage and gain 4 life on turn 1 when the opponent has no board presence worth killing (just a tapped land) is a massive waste of resources. The opponent is at 20 life so 4 damage is minimal, and the life gain is unnecessary at 20 life. This leaves the player with only a Swamp, Undercity Sewers, and whichever two black cards remain - a devastated hand.

With Necrodominance (BBB) in hand and Sheoldred (2BB) also in hand, the player needs black mana sources as fast as possible. Playing Undercity Sewers this turn (which enters tapped) would set it up to produce mana on turn 2, while the Swamp could be played untapped on turn 2 instead. Since the player has no 1-mana plays available this turn anyway (Fatal Push has no target), playing the tapped land now costs nothing in tempo and gets it online sooner. This sequencing matters for casting Necrodominance on turn 3 - the player needs 3 black sources by then, and Undercity Sewers produces black mana. Additionally, Undercity Sewers triggers surveil 1 on entry, which helps fill the graveyard (already has Soul Spike there). Playing the Swamp first means the Sewers must enter tapped on a later turn when the mana might be needed untapped.

Playing Dragon's Rage Channeler before playing Steam Vents is a sequencing error. Steam Vents should be played first (either tapped or paying 2 life) to have access to more mana options. More importantly, playing the land first doesn't cost anything - you can still cast DRC after. Playing the creature before the land means if you draw or need the land for any reason, you've already committed. Additionally, playing Steam Vents untapped (paying 2 life) would give access to 2 mana, enabling Cori-Steel Cutter as a second spell to trigger Flurry on DRC. While this costs 2 more life, the sequencing of land-before-spell is generally correct since there's no reason to cast the creature first.

message: Select a card (To put on the bottom of your library)
annotation_description: Playing Mishra's Bauble before playing Bloodstained Mire is a sequencing error. By playing the land first, Villain would have had access to an additional mana source this turn and could potentially crack the fetchland later. More importantly, playing the land drop first is free and doesn't conflict with casting Bauble. The Bauble doesn't cost mana, but playing the land first ensures the land drop isn't forgotten and maximizes available mana for the turn. Additionally, with Expressive Iteration on the stack resolving, the order matters less, but the general principle of playing lands before spells (especially free ones that don't benefit from being cast first) applies. However, the Bauble was exiled from Expressive Iteration and must be played this turn, so casting it is correct - but the land should have been played first to ensure the land drop isn't missed and to have maximum mana available.

annotation_description: The player should play Bloodstained Mire first before activating Mishra's Bauble. Playing the land costs nothing and doesn't use mana, and it's important to sequence land drops before other actions. If the Bauble is activated first, the land can still be played afterward, so the sequencing issue is minor. However, there's a subtle reason to play Bloodstained Mire first: if the player wants to crack the fetch land this turn (e.g., to enable revolt or fix mana), they'd want to do so after seeing the top card with Bauble. But more importantly, playing the land first preserves maximum flexibility - the player might want to crack the Mire in response to the Bauble activation to shuffle away a bad top card, or sequence things differently based on what they see. Activating Bauble first without the land in play slightly reduces options.

message: Select a Swamp or Mountain card
annotation_description: Fetched Steam Vents instead of basic Mountain when their entire hand is red spells and they already have a Steam Vents on the battlefield for blue mana access. Paying 2 life unnecessarily at 13 life (or entering tapped for no benefit over a basic) is a real cost, especially in an aggressive deck that's taking damage from its own mana base.

With delirium already active (4 card types in opponent's graveyard), Unholy Heat deals 6 damage and is the only card in the opponent's hand that cleanly kills Sheoldred, the Apocalypse (4/5). Taking Slickshot Show-Off instead leaves the opponent with the ability to immediately answer Sheoldred for just 1 mana when it lands on turn 4, which is Sarge's primary game plan.

With 3 mana available (Thundering Falls + 2 Steam Vents), the player could cast Slickshot Show-Off (1R) first, then cast Monastery Swiftspear as the second spell to trigger Slickshot's prowess (+2/+0), giving a bigger attack this turn. Alternatively, casting Monastery Swiftspear first and then a noncreature spell would trigger prowess on Swiftspear, but the player has no 1-mana noncreature spell they'd want to cast precombat without a target (Lightning Bolt could go face but is better saved, Unholy Heat has no target). However, the key consideration is that Slickshot Show-Off has flying and haste - casting it alongside Swiftspear and then casting Lightning Bolt at opponent's face would trigger prowess on both creatures and Slickshot's +2/+0, potentially dealing significantly more damage. With Slickshot (1/2 + 2/0 from its own trigger = 3/2 flying) + Swiftspear (1/2 + 1/1 prowess = 2/3) + 3 from bolt = 8 damage vs just deploying Swiftspear for 1 damage. But spending Lightning Bolt on face turn 4 against a Necrodominance/Sheoldred deck may not be optimal. The sequencing question of Swiftspear vs Slickshot first is interesting but not clearly wrong given the opponent has no blockers and limited mana.

Plotting Slickshot Show-Off uses 2 mana now but delays the creature to a future turn. The opponent has only 2 lands (both tapped) and limited board presence. Casting Slickshot Show-Off directly would give an immediate flying haste attacker that could pressure the opponent's 19 life alongside Monastery Swiftspear, especially since the opponent appears to be developing slowly with a Necrodominance-style deck. Plotting is generally good when you want to cast it for free later alongside multiple spells, but the opponent could find removal or stabilize with Sheoldred. However, plotting does enable a bigger burst turn later where Slickshot comes down free and multiple noncreature spells can pump it significantly, so this is debatable rather than clearly wrong.

Gem25P Villain has Monastery Swiftspear on board and the opponent at 15 life with all lands tapped and no untapped blockers. The opponent has Necrodominance but no creatures. Villain has Lightning Bolt, Lightning Bolt, Unholy Heat, and Cori-Steel Cutter in hand with 4 lands (including 2 Steam Vents and Thundering Falls that produce red). Casting a spell before combat would trigger Prowess on Monastery Swiftspear, increasing damage output. For example, casting Lightning Bolt at the opponent's face (3 damage) plus attacking with a prowess-buffed Swiftspear (2/3) deals 5 damage total, bringing opponent to 10. Even better, casting Cori-Steel Cutter (giving Swiftspear +1/+1, trample, and haste, making it 2/3 base + prowess trigger for 3/4) and then attacking deals more. The opponent is on Necrodominance and will be paying life to draw cards, so every point of damage matters enormously. Passing without casting anything wastes mana and tempo against an opponent who is building toward a powerful late game with Necrodominance.

By casting Inquisition of Kozilek before playing Polluted Delta, Sarge taps one of their three available lands and loses the ability to cast Sheoldred, the Apocalypse this turn. With Polluted Delta played first and cracked for a Swamp, they'd have 4 lands producing BBBB - exactly enough for Sheoldred (2BB). At 9 life against a Slickshot Show-Off burn deck, deploying Sheoldred's 4/5 deathtouch body with lifegain is significantly more impactful than seeing the opponent's hand.

annotation_description: At 8 life facing a 5/2 flying Slickshot Show-Off, Sarge activated Psychic Frog's flying ability (exiling all 3 graveyard cards) but then did not block, taking 5 damage and falling to 3 life. The Frog needed flying to block the flying Show-Off, so the activation was correct, but failing to then actually block was game-losing. Blocking would have traded the 3/4 Frog for the 5/2 Show-Off and prevented 5 damage.

Psychic Frog was given flying by exiling all 3 cards from graveyard, but the opponent has no untapped creatures to block. Flying provides no benefit here. While Necrodominance reduces future graveyard value, those cards are still permanently lost for zero gain.

Villain has lethal on board - Slickshot Show-Off (1/2 flying) can attack Sarge who is at 1 life with no untapped flying blockers. Casting Expressive Iteration before combat is unnecessary and risks potential interaction (Sarge has access to U and B mana from Undercity Sewers and Swamp). Should attack first to secure the kill.

At 1 life facing a Slickshot Show-Off that threatens lethal, Sarge declined to cast March of Wretched Sorrow which would kill the Show-Off (2 damage to a 1/2) and gain 2 life, bringing them to 3. At 1 life, any burn spell or combat damage is lethal, making this removal + lifegain critical for survival.
